extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (agents and attorneys), law firm compliance counsel, and USPTO OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for a USPTO practitioner submitting an Affidavit of Resignation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, and the Office's orders and obligations that follow (exclusion on consent, limited recognition to wind up client matters, publication, notice, and reinstatement rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation requirements (37 C.F.R. §11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must state that the practitioner's resignation is freely and voluntarily rendered, that the practitioner is not being subjected to coercion or duress, and that the practitioner is fully aware of the implications of submitting the resignation; the affidavit waives proceedings before a hearing officer; acknowledges awareness of any pending investigation and that the practitioner does not wish to contest the facts; agrees not to contest the facts set forth (including in any other bar disciplinary, reinstatement, or admission proceeding); acknowledges the right to be represented by counsel; and acknowledges that the practitioner may not petition for reinstatement for five years and that upon any reinstatement application the OED Director will conclusively presume certain facts for purposes of determining reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document examples: the affidavit's enumerated averments (e.g., 'resignation is freely and voluntarily rendered...','waiving proceedings before a hearing officer', 'I do not wish to contest the facts...'). The affidavit must expressly waive hearings and may include a multi-jurisdictional waiver of contesting facts. The affidavit should state understanding of consequences (e.g., compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 after exclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Director authority to approve affidavit and exclude respondent
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to statutes and regulations (e.g., 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27), the USPTO Director has authority to review and approve an Affidavit of Resignation and to enter an order excluding the practitioner on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Director approves an affidavit that complies with § 11.27, the Director may enter an exclusion on consent and provide other appropriate actions (e.g., limited recognition, publication, notice to disciplinary authorities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to wind up client matters (30-day period)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an exclusion on consent is entered, the Director may grant limited recognition to practice before the Office for a specified short period (here, 30 days) solely for the purpose of winding up all client business before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the limited recognition period the practitioner must wind up client business and withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.40, and shall not accept any new clients having business before the Office during that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties and compliance while excluded (37 C.F.R. §11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who is excluded on consent must 'comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58' while excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order requires explicit compliance with the cited regulation; the document itself does not restate §11.58's text but makes compliance a mandatory condition of the exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of discipline (37 C.F.R. §11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order (e.g., in the OED Reading Room and the Official Gazette) and give notice of the public discipline and reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State(s) where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order includes a formal 'Notice of Exclusion on Consent' suitable for publication (the text is reproduced in the order) and cites the OED Reading Room URL for posting; publication and interagency notice are required by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure and presumptions (37 C.F.R. §11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who resigns under § 11.27 may not petition for reinstatement for five years; if and when the practitioner applies for reinstatement under § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the limited purpose of determining the reinstatement application, that (i) the facts upon which the investigation is based are true and (ii) the practitioner could not have successfully defended himself against the allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit should notify the practitioner of the five-year bar and the specific presumptions that will attend any future reinstatement application; the order also requires compliance with § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of ownership or financial interest in third‑party vendors
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must disclose to their firm partners and clients if they own or operate a business entity that provides services (e.g., patent database searches) used by the firm; failure to inform partners or clients of such ownership/operation is a basis for disciplinary investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case example: Respondent formed 'The IP Resource Company' to perform searches and did not inform partners or clients that he was the owner and operator — the omission was central to the investigation and affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Billing practices and invoicing standards (itemization and recordkeeping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invoices submitted for client charges should itemize costs, services rendered, dates services were rendered, and time spent, and practitioners (or their vendors) must maintain underlying billing records so costs and services can be satisfactorily accounted for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern shown: sixty summary-form invoices were submitted that did not itemize costs, services, dates, or time, covering ~3,449 matters and totaling $733,771.30; respondent either did not maintain or did not retain underlying billing records and could not satisfactorily account for costs and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of client payments and prohibition on misappropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not endorse client-paid checks for deposit into accounts for personal use and must be able to account for costs incurred and services rendered; depositing client-paid checks into a personal account and inability to account for the charges constitutes misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case example: respondent endorsed checks paid by the firm for the vendor and caused them to be deposited in an account for his personal use and cannot satisfactorily account for the services — cited as basis for exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies and firm responsibilities upon discovering practitioner misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon discovering that a practitioner engaged in improper billing or undisclosed self-dealing, the firm may (and in practice will) reimburse affected clients in full for improper charges; the Office will publish disciplinary decisions and notify relevant authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document notes the firm 'intends to reimburse all clients in full' for the charges billed by the undisclosed vendor and that disciplinary decisions are posted publicly at the OED Reading Room; publication and client reimbursement are presented as expected remedial actions.
